claims.text: Lightweight HEAs can combine low density, mechanical strength, corrosion resistance, and high-temperature oxidation resistance through a refined dual-phase microstructure.
A refined dual-phase microstructure promotes in situ formation of continuous protective Cr- and Al-rich oxide layers.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion produce or stabilize the proposed refined dual-phase microstructure.
Targeted additions of low-density elements such as Al, Ti, or Mg enable grain refinement and nanoscale precipitation.
Grain refinement and nanoscale precipitates inhibit dislocation motion and crack propagation.
The intended starting alloy contains multiple principal elements, including low-density constituents, Cr, and other refractory elements.
The intended alloy has a dual-phase BCC and FCC structure.
Reducing the number of principal elements lowers configurational entropy.
The full high-entropy alloy and reduced-element comparison alloy can be prepared at similar overall density.
The relevant structural mediator consists of ultrafine grains, nanoscale precipitates, a dual-phase matrix, and a continuous Cr- and Al-rich oxide scale.
The dual-phase matrix impedes dislocation motion and crack propagation.
During high-temperature oxidation, the proposed microstructure enables rapid formation and retention of a continuous, slow-growing protective oxide layer.
The protective oxide layer limits further chemical attack and oxidation.
Relative to the lower-entropy baseline, the full high-entropy alloy will have higher hardness and tensile strength.
Relative to the lower-entropy baseline, the full high-entropy alloy will have lower corrosion rates.
Relative to the lower-entropy baseline, the full high-entropy alloy will have lower oxidation weight gain at 800–900 °C.
The lower-entropy baseline lacks the same degree of microstructural refinement and continuous oxide-scale formation.
The proposed performance advantage may cease when processing produces coarse or segregated phases.
The proposed performance advantage may cease when environmental fluctuations disrupt the oxide scale or when non-protective oxides form.
